issues.explanation: The required body sentence is 'You are invited to join :entity as :role.' (task.md:52-53), but the view renders 'You are invited to :entity as :role.' and lang/pt_BR.json:850 uses the shortened key; tests/Feature/Entity/EntityInviteMailTest.php:47 asserts the shortened text, so the deviation is baked into the test.

Invite creation/cancellation and the accept/decline membership writes are implemented directly in the Livewire components instead of one class per use case under app/Actions/*, as conventions.md requires for domain writes.

closeMember() and cancelRemoval() are public Livewire actions without an authorization check, so a manager who is later demoted can replay a stale component snapshot and trigger a re-render that still returns the entity's member and pending-invite lists.
The race handler only treats SQLSTATE 23000 as a unique violation; on PostgreSQL (SQLSTATE 23505) the same concurrent insert would be rethrown and become a 500 instead of an inviteEmail error.
The modal shell has no Escape-key handling or focus management, so keyboard users can tab behind the dialog; conventions.md asks for accessible modal markup.

review.summary: The change replaces instant member addition with a complete invite flow: entity_invites schema/model/factory, a queued markdown mail, PendingInvites accept/decline, a manager-only members page with detail and removal modals, translations, docs and extensive Pest tests. It is well structured and secure in its sensitive actions; the remaining issues are minor (the invite e-mail omits the required word 'join', the Livewire domain writes bypass the Actions convention, and two public modal actions are not authorized), so it is approvable with small fixes.
